problem.text: The keystone arch is an ancient architectural feature. It is composed of congruent isosceles trapezoids fitted together along the non-parallel sides, as shown. The bottom sides of the two end trapezoids are horizontal. In an arch made with $9$ trapezoids, let $x$ be the angle measure in degrees of the larger interior angle of the trapezoid. What is $x$?

steps.title: Where to start: extend the legs to a common center
steps.body: The trapezoids are congruent and the arch is symmetric, and the two end pieces sit flat on the ground. That is the clue: if you extend every leg (non-parallel side) downward, they all meet at one point $X$ on the ground line, the center of the half-circle. The $9$ trapezoids then cut the straight angle at $X$ into $9$ equal wedges.

your_turn.prompt: How many degrees does each wedge have at $X$?
your_turn.answer: $180^\circ \div 9 = 20^\circ$, since the $9$ equal wedges fill the straight angle along the ground.

steps.title: Each trapezoid sits inside an isosceles triangle
steps.body: Take the right end trapezoid. Let $Y$ be its outer corner on the ground and $Z$ its other outer corner. Its two legs, extended, meet at $X$, so the trapezoid is triangle $XYZ$ with a small triangle cut off near $X$. The angle at $X$ is $20^\circ$. Because the trapezoid is isosceles, its two angles at the long outer side $YZ$ are equal, so triangle $XYZ$ is isosceles with those as its base angles.

your_turn.prompt: The trapezoid's short inner side is parallel to $YZ$. How is the trapezoid's angle at $Y$ related to its angle at the inner corner on the same leg?
your_turn.answer: They add up to $180^\circ$, because they are co-interior angles between two parallel sides.

steps.title: Put it together
steps.body: The base angles of triangle $XYZ$ are $\tfrac{180^\circ - 20^\circ}{2} = 80^\circ$. These are the trapezoid's angles at the outer side; they are acute, so they are the smaller angles. An isosceles trapezoid has only two angle sizes, and the angles at the inner side are $180^\circ - 80^\circ = 100^\circ$. Careful: $80$ is the smaller angle, not the one asked for. So $x = 100$, and the answer is **(A)**.
